basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 15.' and it opens '(Vers. 15.) Et sumpsit Dominus Deus hominem, et posuit eum in paradiso voluptatis. Pro'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 15.) Et sumpsit Dominus Deus hominem, et posuit eum in paradiso voluptatis. Pro voluptate, in Hebraeo habet EDEN. Ipsi igitur nunc Septuaginta EDEN interpretati sunt voluptatem. Symmachus vero qui florentem paulo ante paradisum transtulerat, hic posuit ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ τῆς ἀκτῆς, quod et ipsum amoenitatem et delicias sonat.
